subject: Pilot packaging: burst-credit tranche vs prepaid tranche — options & ask
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Natalie Park <natalie.park@zephyrdynamics.com>
Cc: procurement@zephyrdynamics.com, eng-lead@zephyrdynamics.com
Date: Sun, 9 Nov 2025 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot packaging: burst-credit tranche vs prepaid tranche — options & ask

Hi Natalie — following up from last week's demo. Nice energy from the team. Quick note with two packaging options we can move on today and a short procurement ask so your legal/procurement teams can size timelines. Attached: pilot_scope.pdf (draft scope + metrics).

Option 1 — Burst credit tranche (recommended for quick validation)
- One-time bucket: 50,000 token-equivalent burst credits (usable over 30 days)
- Price: $15,000 one-time purchase (discounted for pilot)
- No long-term commitment; includes basic observability access + 2 support syncs
- If credits exhausted, automatic throttle; can purchase top-up at list price

Option 2 — Prepaid tranche with SLA credit backstop
- Prepaid tranche: $40,000 (60-day runway) with capacity prioritization for bursts
- Includes an SLA credit clause: if 99.5%% latency SLO missed for >3 consecutive hours, 10%% credit applied to next invoice
- Includes onboarding hours (6) and extended telemetry retention (90 days)

Quick asks from your side so we can draft the amendment:
1) Which option is preferred (1 or 2)?
2) Do you need a PO or vendor paperwork before we can issue invoice?
3) Pilot end date flexibility — current sandbox access ends 2025-11-20; would you prefer an explicit 2-week extension or the burst bucket instead?

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow to walk through economics. If you want, we can combine: smaller prepaid tranche + a modest burst bucket.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Natalie Park <natalie.park@zephyrdynamics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@zephyrdynamics.com, eng-lead@zephyrdynamics.com
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: burst-credit tranche vs prepaid tranche — options & ask

Sean — thanks for the clear options. A couple of clarifying q's before procurement loops in: 
- Is the $15k burst bucket refundable/transferable if we graduate to a paid contract within 60 days?
- For Option 2, can the SLA-credit threshold be tightened to 99.0%% availability or is 99.5%% standard for pilot packaging? Our infra team will also want to confirm what "capacity prioritization" actually looks like (is it single-tenant on a dedicated pool or weighted routing?).

Procurement note (from procurement@zephyrdynamics.com): our standard PO turnaround is ~7 business days; we asked for a contact for the invoice.

—Natalie
Natalie Park
Dir., AI Platforms
Zephyr Dynamics

On Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 11:04 AM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks Natalie — quick answers inline: 
> 
> - Burst bucket refundability: we can apply the one-time burst payment as a credit toward a paid contract if you convert within 45 days. It is not refundable in cash but will be fully credited against the first committed invoice.
> - SLA threshold: 99.5%% is our standard pilot backstop; for prepaid tranche we can add a 99.0%% availability threshold if procurement/legal need that tightened, but that would move to a formal SLA appendix.
> - Capacity prioritization: for the prepaid tranche we offer "weighted routing" into a higher-priority pool (not single-tenant) — that gives better tail latency but still shares infra. If you require single-tenant, we should move to a Dedicated discussion (that changes pricing markedly).
> 
> I'll also add david.kim@redwoodinference.com (finance) and marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com (CS lead) to keep timelines tight.
> 
> Sean
>

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: natalie.park@zephyrdynamics.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Pilot packaging: burst-credit tranche vs prepaid tranche — options & ask

Folks — internal quick thread before we lock terms. Natalie has asked about refundability and tighter SLA. My take: convertibility credit is low-risk and a nice accelerator. Proposal suggestions: 
- Offer: 50k burst credits ($15k) -> refundable as a 100%% credit toward first committed contract if signed within 45 days (keeps cash non-refundable but fully applied)
- Prepaid tranche alternative: $35k (vs $40k) if they accept a 10%% reseller-style discount for pilots and we keep SLA at 99.5%% unless procurement insists (we can sign 99.0%% for a one-off)
- For procurement speed, offer a simplified invoice flow (standard vendor pack + our invoice contact: ar.billing@redwoodinference.com)

Agree we should avoid single-tenant promises here. Also, include a 2-week no-cost sandbox extension if they commit to any paid tranche within 7 days of pilot end — helps engineering finish evals.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: natalie.park@zephyrdynamics.com
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 11:18:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Pilot packaging: burst-credit tranche vs prepaid tranche — options & ask

+1 to Marissa's framing. Finance is ok with: 
- Burst bucket creditability into first invoice (45-day conversion window)
- Small pilot discount on prepaid tranche (10%%) if Zephyr provides a PO within 7 business days
- Include standard redline_SLA_v1.docx as the base; any 99.0%% ask requires legal sign-off and we should limit it to prepaid tranche only

I'll prep an invoice template and a one-page amendment we can send to Natalie listing the two options and the conversion mechanics. Sean, can you confirm the exact pilot end date they want extended if they pick the burst bucket? We agreed the sandbox currently expires 2025-11-20.

David
David Kim
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot packaging: burst-credit tranche vs prepaid tranche — options & ask

Natalie — thanks for the quick responses and for looping procurement. Per internal alignment, here are concrete options we can sign/apply tomorrow: 

Finalized options (we can issue the invoice / amendment once you confirm):
A) Burst bucket (quickest path)
- 50,000 token credits, $15,000 one-time
- Credits fully applied to first committed invoice if you convert within 45 days
- No cash refunds
- We will extend sandbox access by 2 weeks (new end date 2025-12-04) if you purchase the burst bucket by 2025-11-14

B) Prepaid tranche (higher capacity guarantee)
- $35,000 (pilot discounted rate; standard $40k) for 60-day tranche
- SLA appendix: 99.5%% availability standard; we will agree to 99.0%% for prepaid tranche only pending legal sign-off
- Includes 6 onboarding hours and extended telemetry retention

Next steps:
- Tell us A or B (or "hybrid") so we can generate the invoice/one-page amendment and route to ar.billing@redwoodinference.com
- If procurement needs any vendor paperwork, cc contracts@redwoodinference.com and we'll prioritize turnaround

If it's helpful, I'm available for a 20-min call tomorrow at 9am PT to finalize.

Appreciate the partnership — excited to get Zephyr a stable evaluation runway.

Best,
Sean
